children.text: Your Patients' Conversations Stay With You

When patients share sensitive health information, they trust you to protect it. Meetily keeps the recording and transcript on your device, and you choose whether summaries run on a local model or with your own API key.

children.q: Does using Meetily make my practice HIPAA compliant?
children.a: No software makes an organization HIPAA compliant on its own, and HIPAA does not certify products. Compliance is a program your organization runs. Meetily is designed for HIPAA-aligned workflows: recording and transcription run on your device, so patient audio is never uploaded, and there is no Meetily cloud storing your transcripts. A local summary model keeps the transcript on the device too; with your own cloud API key, that provider receives the transcript text.

children.q: Can I use an AI meeting assistant for medical meetings?
children.a: Yes, with the right setup. Meetily can transcribe and summarize healthcare discussions on the clinician's computer when you pair local transcription with a local summary model. Cloud transcription services receive the audio, which is why they are usually reviewed as business associates. With Meetily, recordings and transcripts stay on your device and are not sent to Zackriya Solutions. Whether that changes your obligations is a call for your compliance or legal team.

children.q: Can I use AI meeting notes in healthcare without violating HIPAA?
children.a: It depends on how the tool handles PHI and how your organization uses it. Tools that send audio to external servers add another party to the flow of PHI. Meetily keeps recording and transcription on the device, and summaries can run on a local model, so PHI does not have to leave your own systems. Meetily does not replace your policies on access, retention and patient consent, and your organization stays responsible for its own compliance program.

children.q: Do I need a BAA (Business Associate Agreement) with Meetily?
children.a: That is a determination for your compliance or legal team, and we cannot make it for you. What we can describe is the data flow: Meetily records and transcribes on your device, recordings and transcripts are stored there, and Zackriya Solutions does not receive them. If you use a cloud AI provider for summaries with your own API key, that provider receives the transcript text, so check whether you need a BAA with that provider.

children.q: How does Meetily protect PHI during telehealth sessions?
children.a: Meetily captures the call audio and transcribes it with on-device models, so the audio of a virtual visit is never uploaded. The transcript is stored locally. Nothing is sent to an external server unless you choose a cloud AI provider for summaries, in which case that provider receives the transcript text. Pick a local summary model to keep the whole session on the device.

children.q: Is Meetily suitable for mental health and therapy sessions?
children.a: It can be, where confidentiality comes first. Recording and transcription happen on the therapist's computer, so session audio is not transmitted to or stored on external servers. For the strictest setups, use a local summary model so the transcript stays on the device too. Get the patient's consent before recording, and follow your own documentation policies.

children.q: Can hospital IT review how Meetily handles data?
children.a: Yes. The Community Edition is open source (MIT license), so your IT security team can read the code to see how audio is captured, transcribed and stored, and confirm that transcription runs locally. Meetily Pro adds features on top of the same on-device transcription. Your team can then judge whether your setup meets your technical safeguard requirements.

children.q: How do I handle data retention and destruction with Meetily?
children.a: Recordings and transcripts are stored on your device, and you delete meetings in the app or remove the recording files. There is no Meetily cloud copy to request deletion from. If you use a cloud AI provider for summaries, check its retention terms for the transcript text it receives.
